memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Low back pain radiating to left leg, associated numbness; crampy abdominal pain with bloating; seasonal sneezing and nasal congestion.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/82 mmHg, weight 68 kg, height 1.60 m, BMI 26.6 (obese). Straight leg raise positive at 45° left. Abdomen soft, no tenderness. Nasal mucosa pale, turbinates swollen.
IMPRESSION: 1) Sciatica likely lumbar disc irritation. 2) Irritable bowel syndrome, diarrhoea-predominant. 3) Allergic rhinitis, moderate. Lipids and fasting glucose ordered; baseline CBC, stool, tTG-IgA, IgE.
ARRANGEMENTS: Advise weight reduction, low‑impact exercise, high‑fibre diet, avoid NSAIDs on empty stomach. Start pregabalin 75 mg BD, diclofenac 50 mg BD after food, methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD; mebeverine 135 mg BD, ispaghula husk 5 g OD, loperamide 2 mg SOS; cetirizine 10 mg HS, fluticasone nasal spray 1 spray each nostril OD, montelukast 10 mg HS. Order straight leg raise test, MRI lumbar spine, X‑ray lumbar spine, skin prick test, total serum IgE. Return if: new weakness, bowel/bladder change, fever >39°C, rectal bleeding, severe abdominal pain.

tTG‑IgA < 4 U/ml (negative <7).

Fasting lipid profile: Total cholesterol 210 mg/dl (<200 desirable), LDL‑C 130 mg/dl (<100 optimal), HDL‑C 45 mg/dl (>40 male, >50 female), Triglycerides 180 mg/dl (<150).
Fasting blood glucose 98 mg/dl (70-100).

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Straight leg raise test: left leg pain at 40°, right leg negative. No overt motor weakness. Suggestive of L5 radiculopathy.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Back pain improved, occasional leg tingling after long walks; IBS bloating worse after dairy; allergic rhinitis controlled with occasional nocturnal cough.
EXAMINATION: BP 130/84, weight 66 kg, BMI 25.8 (obese). Lumbar paraspinal tenderness mild. Abdomen non‑tender. Nasal mucosa less swollen.
IMPRESSION: Sciatica partially responding; IBS symptoms exacerbated by lactose; allergic rhinitis well‑controlled. Lipids still elevated.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current meds, add atorvastatin 10 mg nightly for LDL. Advise lactose reduction, regular walking, weight target 60 kg. Order repeat lipid profile in 4 weeks. Return if: worsening leg pain, new numbness, chest pain, dyspnoea, severe abdominal pain.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Recurrent epigastric burning after NSAID use; leg pain unchanged; allergic rhinitis mild.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/80, weight 65 kg, BMI 25.3 (overweight). Epigastric tenderness mild. No peritoneal signs.
IMPRESSION: NSAID‑induced gastritis likely contributing to discomfort; sciatica stable; allergic rhinitis intermittent.
ARRANGEMENTS: Stop diclofenac; start celecoxib 100 mg BD after food with pantoprazole 40 mg OD for gastric protection. Continue pregabalin, methylcobalamin, atorvastatin. IBS meds as before. Allergic rhinitis: continue cetirizine HS, fluticasone OD, montelukast HS. Return if: vomiting, melena, worsening leg pain, fever.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Leg pain worsened after lifting heavy boxes at work; IBS diarrhoea episodes increased; allergic rhinitis worse with dry season.
EXAMINATION: BP 132/86, weight 67 kg, BMI 26.2 (obese). Straight leg raise positive at 38° left. Abdomen soft, mild tenderness left lower quadrant. Nasal mucosa pale.
IMPRESSION: Aggravated sciatica possibly due to mechanical strain; IBS flare‑up; allergic rhinitis seasonal.
ARRANGEMENTS: Add topical diclofenac gel 1% BD to affected area; continue oral celecoxib with pantoprazole. Increase pregabalin to 300 mg BD for neuropathic pain. Continue atorvastatin. Advise lumbar support brace, avoid heavy lifting, physiotherapy referral. Return if: new weakness, bowel/bladder disturbance, severe abdominal pain, fever.
